Findings worth carrying forward:
- e.set/e.get on the router event IS the per-request store — several emits in one request share a request_id, a cron emit gets its own. Module state could not do this (per-JSVM).
- emit() needs opts.record (or an explicit org) to resolve the org. A SUPERUSER has no org of their own, so an emitter that only passes {subject:{...}} silently drops superuser actions. Tier A emitters must pass record: e.record.
- Credentials are NOT in IGNORED_FIELDS: 'the password changed' is the signal; SENSITIVE strips only the values.
- Values over 500 chars are truncated with truncated:true — audit_events.changes has a maxSize and the rows can never be deleted.
- opts.app must be the transaction app when emitting from inside a route's runInTransaction (Tier B).

Keyset, not offsets, and the reason is correctness not speed: an append-only feed grows at the end being read from, so ?page=2 shows some rows twice and skips others. The cursor is (created, id) — created alone loses rows written in the same millisecond.

Two details worth remembering: page() fixes sort to '-created,-id' and does NOT accept a sort parameter (it must match the cursor or paging silently returns nonsense), and a fields projection always gets id+created added back or every cursor would be unbuildable.
